{{one source |date=April 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''Cauchy–Euler operator''' is a [[differential operator]] of the form <math>p(x)\cdot{d \over dx}</math><ref>{{cite book|last=Ross|first=Clay C|title=Differential Equations: An Introduction with Mathematica|year=2004|publisher=Springer|isbn=9781441919410}}</ref> for a polynomial&nbsp;''p''. It is named after [[Augustin-Louis Cauchy]] and [[Leonhard Euler]]. The simplest example is that in which ''p''(''x'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''x'', which has eigenvalues ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0,&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;3,&nbsp;... and corresponding eigenfunctions ''x''<sup>''n''</sup>.
